items.item: The eight applications use the selected logo system, typography, palette and graphic language defined by the guide; differences accommodate application purpose without introducing conflicting identities.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The strategy occupies one page and prioritises quiet overnight lodging for adult short-break travellers, including first-time mountain overnight guests. It states A quiet mountain stay, identifies exactly one primary colour with a usable code, and identifies three brand keywords. Supporting colours are allowed, but competing primary codes, missing keywords or positioning the sky activity as the primary offer fail.

Both documents explicitly repeat the strategy's descriptor, primary colour code and all three keywords without substitutions or altered wording. Placement and layout may differ; a visually similar colour without the same written code does not satisfy repetition.

The comparison presents three meaningfully different design directions, each with a logo proposal, typography, palette and Juniper Twin room cue. The guide explicitly chooses one of those directions as the basis for applications, and the presentation identifies that same choice on page one. Mere colour variants, an ambiguous selection or a conflicting opening-page choice fail; export timestamps are not required as evidence.

The guide records the final logo, descriptor lockup, typography, palette and room cues, with RIDGE & DUSK as the lodging parent, Juniper Twin and Larch Double as room types, Sky Welcome as an optional activity, Sky Stories as its conditional replacement, and Night Notes as a guest notebook. The booking document and presentation visibly use the specified hierarchy and lodging name. Different page layouts are allowed; missing definitions or treatment of subordinate names as unrelated brands fails.

An accommodation overview and separate information pages for Juniper Twin and Larch Double provide the inventory and room specifications. Each type has four rooms; the overall stock is eight rooms accommodating sixteen adults. Juniper Twin has two single beds and Larch Double one double bed, each for two adults. Beds and Capacity label the corresponding information. Inventory must not be presented as current availability, and any displayed identifiers must respect J01–J04 and L01–L04.

Compare the printed room names and visual cues with the booking pages and guide. The welcome card and J02 plate identify J02 Juniper Twin and share its defined cue; the other plate identifies L03 Larch Double and uses the corresponding cue. Scaling and application-specific placement are allowed. Swapped room types, incorrect identifiers or incompatible cues fail; an optional graphic symbol is not mandatory.

The booking information associates Check-in with Reception and 15:00–18:00, Check-out with By 10:00, and Quiet hours with the overnight interval 22:00–07:00. These must be readable guest instructions using the local 24-hour convention. Layout may vary; a missing place, altered deadline or interval presented as daytime fails.

The arrival panel and welcome card each show the Reception check-in window 15:00–18:00, Check-out with By 10:00, and Quiet hours 22:00–07:00. The welcome card additionally identifies the already-booked J02 stay for two adults arriving at Reception at 16:00 for one night. The quiet-hours card labels the same overnight interval and carries Please keep voices low. Judge each record on its assigned application; information on another file does not cure an omission.

Each image contains both readable flat rectangular plate artwork for its assigned room and a view of that same plate applied to the existing pale neutral wood door. Viewpoint and framing may vary while the carrier remains recognisable. Missing either view, changing the artwork between views or replacing the door carrier fails.

The booking document includes both specified instructions and explains that reserving a room does not register a guest for the optional activity. Registration is at Reception by 18:00, followed by the arrangement announcement there at 18:30. Missing wording, reversed times or implied automatic enrolment fails.

Each application independently carries both complete instructions, with the deadline tied to activity sign-up and 18:30 tied to the Reception decision announcement. Capitalization and line wrapping may vary. Omission, a changed time or wording that treats room booking as activity registration fails.

Both named cards give 20:30–21:15, twelve places and eligibility for registered overnight guests. Sky Welcome describes a gentle hosted beginner sky introduction at Viewing Terrace, with a shared telescope look conditional on conditions. Sky Stories describes an indoor introductory sky-observing talk at Reading Room and includes the specified condition. Both explain that the indoor arrangement replaces the terrace session for the same registered group. Treating them as two separately bookable sessions, guaranteeing telescope use or changing the group, time or capacity fails.

The deliverable visibly provides flat front-cover artwork for the small guest notebook, with Night Notes readable and RIDGE & DUSK identifiable as its lodging parent. Cover composition may vary. A missing title, missing lodging identity or an interior page in place of cover artwork fails; blank interior pages need not be demonstrated.

Review the complete video and its duration: it runs ten seconds and progresses from daytime arrival to an explicitly optional evening programme, then quiet accommodation. It uses the selected identity and recognisable guest applications, displays RIDGE & DUSK, and ends with A quiet mountain stay. Editing and shot choices may vary, and every application need not appear. A reordered or missing stage, mandatory-activity implication, unrelated identity or missing end-frame descriptor fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least eight pages and visibly reuses recognisable material from every listed source, including each of the eight guest applications. Repositioning, scaling and legible excerpts are allowed. Source names alone, placeholders, unrelated recreations or omission of any source fail.

The accommodation overview itself displays A quiet mountain stay as the lodging descriptor. Its presence only on a room information page or elsewhere in the document does not satisfy the required placement.

Guest-facing copy is English and communicates the assigned information in direct, calm and welcoming language. Short labels and concise instructions are acceptable. Non-English or bilingual public copy, alarmist wording, exaggerated promotional claims or language that obscures practical instructions fails.

The written identity and public-facing examples use English, and guest copy follows the requested calm, welcoming, precise, plain and reassuring voice. No particular logo form, font, colour or room symbol is prescribed before selection. Non-English or bilingual identity copy fails; a freely chosen visual treatment does not fail merely for differing from a reference's styling.

Assess the commissioned surface uses: the Reception panel is flat portrait rectangular artwork for the light interior wall, the room plates are rectangular door applications, and the quiet-hours card is a removable rectangular card suitable for the existing door clip. The panel displays the fixed descriptor. Graphic styling and proportions may vary within these uses; a replacement carrier system, incompatible attachment design or omitted panel descriptor fails. An additional scene mockup is not required for the panel or quiet-hours card.

Treat the materials image as atmospheric guidance rather than a required object or exact palette. The supplied door identity and surface constraints have separate checks. Capitalization and line breaks are permitted typographic variations in public names and labels; the explicitly required exact repetition of strategy facts remains separately checked.

The eight applications use the selected logo system, typography, palette and graphic language defined by the guide; differences accommodate application purpose without introducing conflicting identities. Room names and cues agree with the booking information and guide, including the J02 Juniper Twin and L03 Larch Double pairings. RIDGE & DUSK remains the lodging parent, with room types, the optional activity and its conditional replacement, and Night Notes presented in their defined subordinate roles.

carryThrough.notes: The strategy states the descriptor A quiet mountain stay, one primary colour code and three keywords; the identity guide and presentation repeat all three facts exactly.
The comparison document contains three distinct directions, and the identity guide records one selection before application development; the presentation names that selection on its first page.
